title: Progress 97 Cargo Ship Docking
description:
Watch the unpiloted Roscosmos Progress 97 resupply spacecraft approach the International Space Station after a two-day journey. The spacecraft will autonomously dock at 7:11 a.m. EST (1211 UTC).

For more than 25 years, people have lived and worked continuously aboard the International Space Station, advancing scientific knowledge and making research breakthroughs that aren’t possible on Earth.

The space station helps NASA understand and overcome the challenges of human spaceflight, expand commercial opportunities in low Earth orbit, and build on the foundation for long-duration missions to the Moon, as part of the Artemis program, and to Mars.

Learn more about the International Space Station, its research, and crew at: https://www.nasa.gov/station
creator: NASA

title: Progress 97 Cargo Ship Launch
description:
A spacecraft carrying food, fuel, and supplies is launching to the International Space Station. Watch along with us!

The unpiloted Progress 97 resupply spacecraft is scheduled to lift off at 5:17 a.m. EST (1017 UTC) on Tuesday, Nov. 24, on a Soyuz rocket from the Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan. After liftoff, Progress 97 will travel to the station, a trip that is scheduled to take two days. Once there, it will dock autonomously to the orbiting laboratory. 

For more than 25 years, people have lived and worked continuously aboard the International Space Station, advancing scientific knowledge and making research breakthroughs that aren’t possible on Earth. 

The space station helps NASA understand and overcome the challenges of human spaceflight, expand commercial opportunities in low Earth orbit, and build on the foundation for long-duration missions to the Moon, as part of the Artemis program, and to Mars. 
 
Learn more about the International Space Station, its research, and crew at: https://www.nasa.gov/station
creator: NASA

title: 2026 Thanksgiving Message from the International Space Station
description:
NASA astronauts Anil Menon, Luke Delaney, Jessica Watkins and CSA (Canadian Space Agency) astronaut Josh Kutryk share reflections, well wishes, and meal plans for Thanksgiving while living and working aboard the International Space Station as part of Expedition 75.
 
For more than 26 years, people have lived and worked continuously aboard the International Space Station, advancing scientific knowledge and making research breakthroughs not possible on Earth.
 
Get regular updates from the space station: https://www.nasa.gov/blogs/spacestation/

Download this video: https://go.nasa.gov/4jxMLp9
creator: NASA

title: The Europa Concept (Official NASA+ Trailer)
description:
What mysteries await on Europa?

This moon of Jupiter has long been thought to potentially hold life beneath its icy surface. A new mission, Europa Clipper, is on its way to look for answers — but getting it there has required relentless innovation and overcoming extraordinary challenges.

The Europa Concept is coming to YouTube in December. Watch it now on NASA+: https://plus.nasa.gov/video/the-europa-concept/ 
Learn more about this documentary: https://nasa.gov/europaconcept

Download this video: https://images.nasa.gov/details/The%20Europa%20Concept
creator: NASA

title: NASA's SpaceX 35th Commercial Resupply Services Undocking
description:
Watch as a SpaceX Dragon spacecraft undocks from the International Space Station and begins its journey back to Earth. The uncrewed Dragon is carrying scientific research samples and hardware including a 3D-bioprinted blood vessel construct and frozen microbial samples.

The spacecraft will reenter Earth's atmosphere Nov. 21 and will splash down off the Californian coast at approximately 5:04 p.m. EST (2:04 p.m. PST, 2204 UTC).

Learn more about NASA's SpaceX CRS-35 mission: https://www.nasa.gov/mission/nasas-spacex-crs-35/
Get daily updates from the space station: https://www.nasa.gov/blogs/spacestation/
creator: NASA

title: Voyager 1 Light-Day Mission Update and Conversation
description:
We're making history with our Voyager spacecraft. Join us for the latest updates.

In this discussion, NASA leadership and mission members will discuss the status of Voyager 1 and 2, the unique science the twin probes are gathering in interstellar space, and the challenges of keeping them operating for so long over such vast distances. 

Stick around for a Q&A with media and other audience members, as well as a preview of the upcoming NASA+ Voyager documentary planned for release in 2027 for the mission's 50th anniversary.

Participants include:
- Nicky Fox, associate administrator, Science Mission Directorate, NASA Headquarters
- Jonathan Lunine, chief scientist, NASA JPL, and professor of planetary science, Caltech
- Suzanne Dodd, Voyager project manager, NASA JPL
- Linda Spilker, Voyager project scientist, NASA JPL
- Kareem Badaruddin, Voyager mission manager, NASA JPL
- Jamie Rankin, Voyager deputy project scientist, Princeton University

Voyager 1, the most distant human-made object from Earth, will have traveled one light-day (more than 16 billion miles) as of Wednesday, Nov. 18. Learn more about the milestone: https://www.nasa.gov/news-release/nasa-invites-media-public-to-join-voyager-1-one-light-day-activities/

Learn more about NASA's Voyager mission: https://science.nasa.gov/mission/voyager/
creator: NASA

title: Who Can Be a NASA Astronaut? Myth or Fact
description:
Who can be a NASA astronaut? The answer may be different than you think.

Applications for astronaut candidates are open until Dec. 3, and we want you to apply! Our current class of astronaut candidates is here to bust some common eligibility myths.

Could you be one of our next astronauts? Apply here: https://go.nasa.gov/astro2026

Download this video: https://go.nasa.gov/4fzJBPg
creator: NASA

title: MAX POWER: Highlights from NASA’s First-Ever Tech Expo and Air Show
description:
Relive the best moments from MAX POWER, NASA's first-ever tech expo and air show at and around Kennedy Space Center in Florida.

Thousands gathered over several days in early November for NASA's first exhibition of America's superiority in space, aeronautics, and technology. The family-friendly event honored the nation's 250th anniversary and capped off the agency's Inspiration Tour.

Highlights from the first-ever MAX POWER included flyovers, a skydive by NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman, and a visit from President Donald J. Trump. NASA also unveiled a new X-plane, opened recruitment for astronaut candidates, and launched a student Moon Base challenge, while sharing the agency’s latest lunar exploration plans.

Learn more:
https://www.nasa.gov/maxpower/
https://www.nasa.gov/general/max-power-nasas-inaugural-aerospace-expo-ignites-americas-future/

Download this video: https://images.nasa.gov/details/MAX%20POWER%20Highlights%20from%20NASA's%20First-Ever%20Tech%20Expo%20and%20Air%20Show
creator: NASA

title: NASA Moon Base: November 2026 Update (Nov. 7, 2026)
description:
Join us live from the MAX POWER aerospace expo as we provide an update on our upcoming Moon Base near the lunar South Pole.

Participants in this news conference, taking place at NASA's Kennedy Space Center, include:

- NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman
- Carlos García-Galán, manager, Moon Base Program
- Nicky Fox, associate administrator for Science, NASA Headquarters
- Dayna Ise, acting director, Utility and Infrastructure Office, Moon Base Program

Learn more about this weekend's MAX POWER events: https://go.nasa.gov/4knRFWI
Learn more about Moon Base: https://www.nasa.gov/moonbase/
creator: NASA

title: NASA Expands Lunar Delivery Network to Support Moon Base Development
description:
Establishing a sustained human presence on the Moon will require a steady flow of scientific instruments, new technologies, equipment, and infrastructure to the lunar surface.
 
NASA has selected eight American companies for the next phase of its CLPS (Commercial Lunar Payload Services) initiative, expanding the network of commercial providers eligible for future lunar delivery missions.
 
Building on NASA's existing lunar delivery capabilities, this expansion will help increase the frequency of deliveries to the lunar surface and support the growing demands of Moon Base development.
 
With each lunar delivery, NASA is building toward a future of sustained human exploration and scientific discovery on the Moon.
 
Learn more about Moon Base: https://www.nasa.gov/moonbase/
creator: NASA

title: Become a NASA Astronaut!
description:
Applications are now open to join NASA's astronaut corps. Join us as we expand the frontiers of discovery in low Earth orbit, on the Moon, and beyond. Apply by Dec. 3.

Learn more: https://go.nasa.gov/3XbPprW
creator: NASA

title: Apply to Become A NASA Astronaut
description:
The universe is calling. Will you answer?

For the first time since 2024, applications are open to join NASA's astronaut corps, who will expand the frontiers of discovery as we build a permanent presence on the Moon and prepare for humanity to explore Mars.

Get the details: https://go.nasa.gov/3XbPprW
Start your application: https://www.usajobs.gov/job/891970300

Learn more about what it takes to apply: https://www.nasa.gov/humans-in-space/astronauts/become-an-astronaut/

Applications are due by Thursday, Dec. 3.
creator: NASA

title: U.S. Spacewalk 101
description:
On Thursday, Nov. 5, NASA astronaut Anil Menon and CSA (Canadian Space Agency) astronaut Joshua Kutryk will install and deploy the eighth and final International Space Station Roll-Out Solar Array (IROSA), completing the space station's power system augmentation. Together, the eight roll-out arrays will increase the station's available power by up to 30%. 

The spacewalk is scheduled to begin at 8:30 a.m. EST (1330 UTC) and will last around six and a half hours.

Learn more about this spacewalk: https://go.nasa.gov/4yRBm97
Get daily updates from the space station: https://www.nasa.gov/blogs/spacestation/
creator: NASA

title: Astronaut Anil Menon Speaks With Mark Rober From the International Space Station
description:
Join us as NASA astronaut Anil Menon, currently aboard the International Space Station, speaks with Mark Rober of the ClassCrunchLabs Foundation in advance of National STEM Day.

During this live event, Rober and Menon will discuss questions submitted by students about the station and life in space. Menon will also demonstrate how everyday activities, from eating to experimenting, change in microgravity.

Learn more about how your school or community could speak with astronauts aboard the station: https://www.nasa.gov/stemonstation
creator: NASA

title: U.S. Spacewalk 100
description:
Join us for a spacewalk milestone!

NASA astronaut Anil Menon and CSA (Canadian Space Agency) astronaut Joshua Kutryk are participating in the 100th spacewalk conducted from the International Space Station's Quest airlock without the space shuttle present. This will be the 285th spacewalk conducted to build, maintain, and upgrade the orbiting laboratory.

Menon and Kutryk are expected to begin their spacewalk at about 8:00 a.m. EDT (1200 UTC); they'll be installing a new International Space Station Roll-Out Solar Array (IROSA), which will boost the station's power.

Learn more about today's spacewalk: https://go.nasa.gov/4yRBm97
Get daily updates from the space station: https://www.nasa.gov/blogs/spacestation/
creator: NASA

title: Artemis Acceleration (Oct. 23, 2026)
description:
Tune in as agency leaders provide an update on NASA's plans to return American astronauts to the surface of the Moon by 2028. 

Participants include:
- NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman
- NASA Associate Administrator Amit Kshatriya
- Jeremy Parsons, NASA’s Artemis program manager

As part of a Golden Age of innovation and exploration, NASA will send Artemis astronauts on increasingly difficult missions near the lunar South Pole to explore more of the Moon than ever before. In addition to providing economic benefits and advancing scientific discovery through its Moon missions, NASA will establish an enduring human presence on the lunar surface and build on the agency’s foundation for the first crewed mission to Mars.

More about the Artemis program: https://www.nasa.gov/humans-in-space/artemis/
creator: NASA

title: U.S. Spacewalk Preview News Conference (Oct. 20, 2026)
description:
We're giving a preview of two upcoming spacewalks on Oct. 29 and Nov. 5 to finish installing solar arrays that will provide more power to the International Space Station. 

NASA astronaut Anil Menon and CSA (Canadian Space Agency) astronaut Joshua Kutryk will participate in both spacewalks. The spacewalks will be the 285th and 286th conducted in support of space station assembly, maintenance, and upgrades.

NASA participants in the news conference include:
- Gaurang Patel, operations integration manager, Low Earth Orbit Program
- Garrett Hehn, spacewalk flight director, Flight Operations Directorate

Learn more about the spacewalks: https://go.nasa.gov/4yRBm97
Learn more about International Space Station operations and research: https://www.nasa.gov/station
creator: NASA

title: NASA Moon Base: Rovers and Lunar Terrain Vehicles (October 2026 Update)
description:
There's a lot of ground to cover when you're building a Moon Base. 

From robotic rovers exploring the rugged lunar landscape to lunar terrain vehicles carrying Artemis astronauts across the surface, mobility will play a crucial role in establishing an enduring human presence on the Moon.

During the early phases of Moon Base development, these vehicles will help NASA investigate the lunar South Pole region, conduct scientific research, test new technologies, and gather the information that will inform future missions.

In this Moon Base update, get a closer look at some of the lunar terrain vehicles and robotic rovers helping pave the way for humanity's first lunar outpost. 

Learn more about these vehicles: https://www.nasa.gov/missions/moon-base/nasa-provides-progress-update-on-moon-base-rovers/
Learn more about Moon Base: https://www.nasa.gov/moonbase/ 
Download this video: https://images.nasa.gov/details/Moon_Base_Update-Oct-Lunar_Rovers

[0:00] Introduction 
[0:46] Lunar Rovers 
[1:32] VIPER 
[4:43] The Time of Apollo 
[5:15] Lunar Terrain Vehicle (LTV) 
[8:48] Outro
creator: NASA

title: NASA's SpaceX Crew-12 Postflight News Conference (Oct. 15, 2026)
description:
After spending over seven months in space, members of NASA’s SpaceX Crew-12 will discuss their mission aboard the International Space Station during a news conference at the agency’s Johnson Space Center in Houston.

NASA astronauts Jessica Meir and Jack Hathaway, ESA (European Space Agency) astronaut Sophie Adenot, and Roscosmos cosmonaut Andrey Fedyaev returned to Earth on Oct. 8, after spending 237 days living and working in orbit. (Adenot will return to Europe and not be available during the news conference.)

Learn more about Crew-12's science and technology research: https://go.nasa.gov/4jdAre7

Watch Crew-12's return to Earth: https://youtube.com/live/x6p9Ri0DlNE

Read more about Crew-12's return and today's event: https://go.nasa.gov/3UikER9
creator: NASA

title: NASA's SpaceX 35th Commercial Resupply Services Rendezvous and Docking
description:
Following a successful launch on Oct. 13, 2026, an uncrewed SpaceX Dragon cargo spacecraft will plan to rendezvous with and dock to the International Space Station. The spacecraft, which is carrying over 6,300 pounds of supplies, is scheduled to dock autonomously at about 10:30 a.m. EDT (1430 UTC).

In addition to cargo for the crew aboard the space station, Dragon will deliver several new science experiments that could help restore vision for people on Earth with artificial eye retinas, develop more realistic heart tissue models for disease research, and identify new treatment targets for diseases like Alzheimer’s, Parkinson’s, and multiple sclerosis.

Dragon is scheduled to remain at the space station for one month before undocking and splashing down off the coast of California.

Learn more about the mission: https://www.nasa.gov/general/nasas-spacex-35th-commercial-resupply-mission-overview/

Learn more about International Space Station operations and research: https://www.nasa.gov/station
creator: NASA

title: Planetary Defenders: This Is Not an Exercise
description:
When a newly discovered asteroid posed a potential risk to Earth, a global planetary defense system was put to the test like never before. 

Planetary Defenders: This Is Not an Exercise tells the story of how NASA, its international partners, the astronomy community, and scientists around the world raced to observe and track the asteroid, understand its orbit into the future, calculate its impact probabilities, and eventually retire it from the risk list.

Learn more about NASA’s efforts to find, track and monitor near-Earth asteroids: https://science.nasa.gov/planetary-defense/
Download this episode: https://images.nasa.gov/details/NHQ_2026_0928_Planetary%20Defenders%20This%20Is%20Not%20an%20Exercise
Watch the debut episode of "Planetary Defenders": https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jOb2DQWvDvc
creator: NASA

title: NASA's SpaceX 35th Commercial Resupply Services Launch
description:
Tune in as a new shipment of science and supplies lifts off to the International Space Station.

NASA and SpaceX are targeting 6:33 a.m. EDT (1033 UTC), Tuesday, Oct. 13, for the next cargo launch of SpaceX's Dragon spacecraft to the space station. Dragon will lift off from Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida and is scheduled to dock autonomously at around 11:00 a.m. EDT (1500 UTC) on Thursday, Oct. 15, to the space-facing port of the station’s Harmony module.

Learn more about the mission and the launch timeline: https://go.nasa.gov/3WhHUPG
creator: NASA

title: NASA's Northrop Grumman Commercial Resupply Services 24 Departure
description:
Watch Northrop Grumman’s Cygnus XL spacecraft undock and depart from the International Space Station. 

Flight controllers on the ground will send commands for the space station’s Canadarm2 robotic arm to detach the Cygnus XL spacecraft from the Unity module’s Earth-facing port and maneuver it into position for release at 12:45 p.m. EDT (1645 UTC). 

This Cygnus XL previously delivered more than 11,000 pounds of supplies, science experiments, and other cargo to the space station.

Learn more about this NASA commercial resupply mission: https://www.nasa.gov/mission/nasas-northrop-grumman-crs-24/
creator: NASA

title: NASA's SpaceX Crew-12 Re-Entry & Splashdown
description:
Welcome Crew-12 back to Earth with us!

NASA astronauts Jessica Meir and Jack Hathaway, ESA (European Space Agency) astronaut Sophie Adenot, and Roscosmos cosmonaut Andrey Fedyaev are scheduled to splash down off the coast of California at 11:34 a.m. EDT (1534 UTC) on Thursday, Oct. 8.

We'll have live coverage from re-entry to recovery. Crew-12 spent 235 days on the International Space Station and orbited Earth nearly 3,800 times.

Learn more about what Crew-12 studied during their time in space: https://go.nasa.gov/4z5jVl6
Get the latest updates from the space station: https://www.nasa.gov/blogs/spacestation/
creator: NASA

title: NASA's SpaceX Crew-12 Undocking
description:
Watch the four members of NASA's SpaceX Crew-12 mission — NASA astronauts Jessica Meir and Jack Hathaway, ESA (European Space Agency) astronaut Sophie Adenot, and Roscosmos cosmonaut Andrey Fedyaev — set off to return to Earth. The SpaceX Dragon spacecraft will undock from the International Space Station at approximately 8:05 a.m. EDT (1205 UTC). 

Splashdown is scheduled to occur off the coast of California on Thursday, Oct. 8 at 11:34 a.m. EDT (1534 UTC).

During their nearly eight months aboard the space station, Crew-12 conducted hundreds of hours of scientific research. Their work included testing stem cell production for cell‑based therapies, examining how physical characteristics may affect blood flow during spaceflight, and demonstrating the on‑demand generation of IV fluid for future missions.
 
Learn more about the Crew-12 mission: https://www.nasa.gov/mission/nasas-spacex-crew-12/
Follow the latest Crew-12 updates: https://www.nasa.gov/blogs/crew-12/
creator: NASA

title: NASA's SpaceX Crew-12 Hatch Close
description:
Watch as NASA astronauts Jessica Meir and Jack Hathaway, ESA (European Space Agency) astronaut Sophie Adenot, and Roscosmos cosmonaut Andrey Fedyaev begin final preparations for their return to Earth aboard a SpaceX Dragon spacecraft. 

After the four enter the spacecraft, the hatch is scheduled to close at 6:20 a.m. EDT (1020 UTC). The Dragon is scheduled to undock at 8:05 a.m. EDT (1205 UTC).

Crew-12’s splashdown is targeted for Thursday, Oct. 8 at 11:34 a.m. EDT (1534 UTC).
 
Learn more about the Crew-12 mission: https://www.nasa.gov/mission/nasas-spacex-crew-12/
Follow the latest Crew-12 updates: https://www.nasa.gov/blogs/crew-12/
creator: NASA

title: From the Moon to the 50-Yard Line
description:
From the Moon to the 50-yard line.
 
Six months ago, NASA astronaut Christina Koch flew Philadelphia Eagles Super Bowl confetti around the Moon on the Artemis II mission. Yesterday, in a full circle moment, she served as honorary captain at an Eagles game, bringing a little Moon Joy to the field.
 
#ArtemisII #FlyEaglesFly #MoonJoy
creator: NASA

title: NASA’s SpaceX Crew-12 Farewell and International Space Station Change of Command
description:
Watch as the members of NASA's SpaceX Crew-12 mission – NASA astronauts Jessica Meir and Jack Hathaway, ESA (European Space Agency) astronaut Sophie Adenot, and Roscosmos cosmonaut Andrey Fedyaev – sum up their experiences aboard the International Space Station and say goodbye to the space station crew. Meir will also transfer command of the orbiting laboratory to Roscosmos cosmonaut Pyotr Dubrov.

Learn more about Crew-12: https://www.nasa.gov/mission/nasas-spacex-crew-12/
creator: NASA

title: NASA's SpaceX Crew-13 Arrival & Welcome Remarks
description:
Watch as four explorers arrive at the International Space Station.

After lifting off from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station on Thursday, Oct. 1, at 11:10 a.m. EDT (1510 UTC), Crew-13's spacecraft is scheduled to dock at the orbiting lab at 7 p.m. EDT (2300 UTC), with hatches opening at about 8:45 p.m. EDT (0045 UTC Oct. 2). The crew will also give welcome remarks around 9:20 p.m. EDT (0120 UTC Oct. 2).

NASA astronauts Jessica Watkins and Luke Delaney, CSA (Canadian Space Agency) astronaut Joshua Kutryk, and Roscosmos cosmonaut Sergey Teteryatnikov will spend the next several months in low Earth orbit on NASA's SpaceX Crew-13 mission. 

While there, they will conduct various science experiments and technology demonstrations to benefit life on Earth and in orbit, furthering humanity's journey back to the Moon, to Mars, and beyond.

Learn more about the Crew-13 mission: https://www.nasa.gov/mission/nasas-spacex-crew-13/
Read daily updates from the space station: https://www.nasa.gov/blogs/spacestation/
creator: NASA

title: NASA's SpaceX Crew-13 Postlaunch News Conference (Oct. 1, 2026)
description:
After the successful launch of NASA’s SpaceX Crew-13 mission, leaders discuss the mission and answer questions from media.

Participants include:
- NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman
- Dr. Lori Glaze, associate administrator, Human Spaceflight Mission Directorate, NASA Headquarters 
- Dana Weigel, manager, Low Earth Orbit Program, NASA Johnson 
- Mathieu Caron, director, Astronauts, Life Sciences, and Space Medicine, CSA 
- Julianna Scheiman, director, NASA Science and Dragon Programs, SpaceX

NASA astronauts Jessica Watkins and Luke Delaney, CSA (Canadian Space Agency) astronaut Joshua Kutryk, and Roscosmos cosmonaut Sergey Teteryatnikov launched to the International Space Station (ISS) at 11:10 a.m. EDT (1510 UTC) on Thursday, Oct. 1. They are expected to arrive at the space station around 7 p.m. EDT (2300 UTC). 

While there, the Crew-13 members will conduct various experiments and technology demonstrations to benefit life on Earth and in orbit, furthering our journey back to the Moon, to Mars, and beyond.

Learn more about the ISS: https://www.nasa.gov/reference/international-space-station/
Get updates on Crew-13: https://www.nasa.gov/blogs/crew-13/
creator: NASA

title: NASA's SpaceX Crew-13 Launch
description:
Four new crew members are heading to the International Space Station!

NASA astronauts Jessica Watkins and Luke Delaney, CSA (Canadian Space Agency) astronaut Joshua Kutryk, and Roscosmos cosmonaut Sergey Teteryatnikov are lifting off aboard a SpaceX Dragon spacecraft to spend several months living, working, and conducting scientific research in low Earth orbit.

NASA's SpaceX Crew-13 mission is scheduled to lift off from Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida at 11:10 a.m. EDT (1510 UTC) on Thursday, Oct. 1. The four members of Crew-13 will arrive at the space station later that day.

Learn more about the Crew-13 mission: https://www.nasa.gov/mission/nasas-spacex-crew-13/
Get daily updates from the station: https://www.nasa.gov/blogs/spacestation/
creator: NASA

title: NASA's SpaceX Crew-13 Prelaunch News Conference (Sept. 30, 2026)
description:
Mission experts give a preview of NASA's SpaceX Crew-13 mission to the International Space Station ahead of its launch.

Participants include:
- Dr. Lori Glaze, associate administrator, Human Spaceflight Mission Directorate, NASA Headquarters
- Dana Weigel, manager, Low Earth Orbit Program, NASA Johnson
- Mathieu Caron, director, Astronauts, Life Sciences, and Space Medicine, CSA
- William Gerstenmaier, vice president, Build and Flight Reliability, SpaceX

Crew-13 is scheduled to launch at 11:10 a.m. EDT (1510 UTC), Thursday, Oct. 1, from Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida, with docking planned for about 7 p.m. EDT (2300 UTC). 

The SpaceX Dragon spacecraft will carry Jessica Watkins and Luke Delaney, CSA (Canadian Space Agency) astronaut Joshua Kutryk, and Roscosmos cosmonaut Sergey Teteryatnikov to the International Space Station for a long-duration science mission.

Learn more about Crew-13: https://www.nasa.gov/mission/nasas-spacex-crew-13
creator: NASA

title: NASA's SpaceX Crew-13 Mission (Official NASA Trailer)
description:
NASA astronauts Jessica Watkins and Luke Delaney, CSA (Canadian Space Agency) astronaut Joshua Kutryk, and Roscosmos cosmonaut Sergey Teteryatnikov are scheduled to lift off to the International Space Station on Thursday, Oct. 1.

Once they arrive, they'll spend the next several months in orbit, helping us learn how to live in space while running scientific experiments to make life better back on Earth. Watch the live launch with us here on YouTube.

More info on our Crew-13 launch schedule: https://go.nasa.gov/3V9NKT0
Download this video: https://go.nasa.gov/4zaz3Of
creator: NASA

title: Space Station Operations Update (Sept. 28, 2026)
description:
Leaders from NASA and Boeing hold a news conference at NASA's Kennedy Space Center to provide updates on Starliner development and plans for crew flights to and from the International Space Station. 

Briefing participants include:
 
* NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman
* Dana Weigel, manager, NASA’s Low Earth Orbit Program
* Woody Hoburg, NASA astronaut
* John Mulholland, vice president and program manager, Boeing Commercial Crew

Learn more about the Commercial Crew Program: https://www.nasa.gov/commercialcrew
Get daily updates from the station: https://www.nasa.gov/blogs/spacestation/
creator: NASA

title: Progress 96 Cargo Ship Docking
description:
Watch live as the unpiloted Progress 96 resupply spacecraft docks autonomously to the International Space Station. Docking is set to happen around 9:46 a.m. EDT (1346 UTC).

Progress 96 began its three-day journey to the Space Station on Wednesday, Sept. 16, when it lifted off aboard a Soyuz rocket from the Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan. The spacecraft will remain docked for about five months before departing for a reentry into Earth's atmosphere to dispose of trash loaded by the space station crew.

For more than 25 years, people have lived and worked continuously aboard the International Space Station, advancing scientific knowledge and making research breakthroughs that aren’t possible on Earth. 

The space station helps NASA understand and overcome the challenges of human spaceflight, expand commercial opportunities in low Earth orbit, and build on the foundation for long-duration missions to the Moon, as part of the Artemis program, and to Mars. 
 
Learn more about the International Space Station, its research, and crew at: https://www.nasa.gov/station
creator: NASA

title: NASA’s SpaceX Crew-12 Pre-Departure News Conference (Sept. 16, 2026)
description:
Tune in as the four members of NASA's SpaceX Crew-12 — NASA astronauts Jessica Meir and Jack Hathaway, ESA (European Space Agency) astronaut Sophie Adenot, and Roscosmos cosmonaut Andrey Fedyaev — join us from orbit to recap their mission ahead of their upcoming return to Earth.

During their time aboard the International Space Station, the members of Crew-12 conducted various science experiments and technology demonstrations to benefit life on Earth and in orbit, furthering our journey back to the Moon, to Mars, and beyond.

Learn more about the Crew-12 mission: https://www.nasa.gov/mission/nasas-spacex-crew-12/
Follow the latest Crew-12 updates: https://www.nasa.gov/blogs/crew-12/

Credit: NASA
creator: NASA

title: Progress 96 Cargo Ship Launch
description:
A spacecraft carrying food, fuel, and supplies is launching to the International Space Station. Watch along with us.

The unpiloted Progress 96 resupply spacecraft is scheduled to lift off at 9:33 a.m. EDT (1333 UTC) on Wednesday, Sept. 16, on a Soyuz rocket from the Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan. After liftoff, Progress 96 will travel to the station, a trip that is scheduled to take two days. Once there, it will dock autonomously to the orbiting laboratory. 

For more than 25 years, people have lived and worked continuously aboard the International Space Station, advancing scientific knowledge and making research breakthroughs that aren’t possible on Earth. 

The space station helps NASA understand and overcome the challenges of human spaceflight, expand commercial opportunities in low Earth orbit, and build on the foundation for long-duration missions to the Moon, as part of the Artemis program, and to Mars. 
 
Learn more about the International Space Station, its research, and crew at: https://www.nasa.gov/station

Credit: NASA
creator: NASA

title: NASA Moon Base: The First Six Months
description:
No aim is too high. No journey is too far. No challenge is too tough. 

Since NASA announced plans for a Moon Base in March 2026, work has been moving quickly to turn an ambitious vision into reality. From identifying commercial partners to sending humans around the Moon for the first time in decades, we are advancing the missions, technologies, and capabilities that will help build humanity’s first lunar outpost.

We’re going back to the Moon. This time, to stay. 

Learn more about the Moon Base: https://nasa.gov/moonbase 
Download this video: https://images.nasa.gov/details/NASA_Moon_Base-First_Six_Months 

Credit: NASA
creator: NASA
